title: Multi-Org Product Catalog: Live Federation vs Local Replicas

steps.prompt: A company runs four Salesforce orgs. The NA org masters the product catalog, and CPQ in each regional org reads product records many times during every quote calculation. Price changes must reach every region within five minutes, and two more regional orgs launch next year. How should the architect distribute catalog changes?

options.label: Publish product changes as platform events that a Pub/Sub API client applies to each org
options.rationale: Publish/subscribe lets one change reach many consumers without coupling the source to each of them, so the two new orgs add subscribers rather than NA code changes. Each regional org keeps local copies, so repeated quote-time reads never leave the org.

options.label: Have a Queueable job in the NA org call each regional org's REST API in turn
options.rationale: Every new regional org means changing and redeploying NA code, and one slow or unavailable org delays the updates queued behind it.

options.label: Expose NA product records in each regional org through the Salesforce Connect cross-org adapter
options.rationale: External objects fetch data with a real-time callout on each access, so every repeated product read during a quote calculation waits on the NA org.

options.label: Copy changed products to each regional org with a nightly Bulk API 2.0 job
options.rationale: A nightly job leaves regional quotes on old prices for up to a day, far outside the five-minute window.
